description: I’m Tarjinder Tarun, an electronics & robotics engineer, trainer, and independent researcher with 26+ years of hands-on experience in robotics, electronics, IoT, AI, and innovation. I enjoy turning ideas into practical prototypes and solving real-world problems. I’m looking for team members skilled in AI/ML, data science, software, space science, and creative problem-solving.
summary:
AptaSoil is a smart farming tool that tells farmers when their soil is tired and what to plant next. It was built by Team Mobotics for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, under the guidance of lead R&D architect Tarjinder Tarun and Antonia Georgieva.
The problem: when farmers grow the same cereal crop year after year, a natural chemical called ferulic acid builds up in the soil. This harms the roots and lowers the harvest. This is called soil fatigue.
Our solution: AptaSoil combines two sources of information. From space, it uses NASA satellite data on soil moisture, plant health, sunlight and temperature. From the ground, it uses a small sensor that detects ferulic acid directly in the soil. The app mixes both into one Soil Fatigue Index, a score from 0 to 100.
When the score is high, the app suggests what to do. Its AI crop advisor ranks more than 30 crops and recommends soil-friendly choices such as legumes (which add nitrogen to the soil) and cover crops. Users can also view a satellite map, see a 3D picture of how the sensor works, and download a report as a PDF or CSV file.
By connecting NASA space data with everyday farming, AptaSoil helps farmers protect their land and keep food production strong.
details:
• Satellite Data from Space: The app collects NASA data on soil moisture, plant health, sunlight and temperature for the farmer's location.
  • Soil Sensor: A small electrode coated with a short piece of DNA, called an aptamer. The aptamer sticks to ferulic acid, the toxin that builds up in tired soil. The grip is very tight (Kd=14.2 nM).
  • Soil Fatigue Index (SFI): Combines the satellite and sensor data into one easy score from 0 to 100. The score uses this formula: SFI=Wfa(FA)+Wndvi(1-NDVI)+Wsm(SMAP)
  • AI Crop Advisor: When the soil fatigue score is too high, the app updates how suitable each of more than 30 crops is. It then suggests nitrogen-fixing legumes, cover crops and biofumigation (using certain plants to help clean the soil) so the soil can recover.

Innovation Highlights

  • 📖 Clear Story: The dashboard guides users step by step, from satellite data in space down to the tiny sensor in the soil.
  • 🔭 Easy to Learn From: Complex science is shown in simple visuals that students, farming groups and researchers can understand.
  • 🎨 Simple Design: A clean white and navy look, with NASA blue and red accents, that is easy to read and works on different screen sizes.
  • 📡 Trusted Data: All satellite information comes directly from NASA sources: SMAP, MODIS and NASA POWER.
  • 🧬 Big and Small Together: Links the big picture from satellites with tiny measurements from the soil sensor.

Technology Stack & Tools

  • Website and Design: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, JavaScript and Font Awesome icons are used to build a clean, easy-to-read dashboard.
    • Gemini: AI assistant that helped us write code and plan how the app is organised.
    • ChatGPT: AI assistant that helped us refine prompts, explain the science and draft documentation.
    • Aptadiff: Software that tests, on a computer, how well our DNA sensor sticks to ferulic acid.

Intended Impact & Benefits

AptaSoil aims to protect the food supply and support healthier farming by stopping soil damage in farming regions across North Africa, South Asia and Europe. By helping farmers move away from growing the same crop every season and toward data-based crop rotation, AptaSoil helps bring back healthy soil life, avoid sudden drops in harvest, and keep land productive for the long term.
